title: The Lake Michigan excursion boats and the drummer Tom
summary: He played on the North Shore excursion boat. The pay was a dollar plus $16-17 a night in tips. Tom, a New Orleans musician, later quit for the steel mill.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Didn't you play on an excursion boat on the Lake Michigan?
I heard about that. I heard about that. These people from the archives told me about that. Yeah. Sweet Williams.

Yeah. On a boat. Didn't get no pay there. No? No. Just tip. They give you one dollar to come down for coffee. Oh. And, well, as it rained the boat didn't go out. It was a boat go out in the lake and come back. You know, go to Jackson Park out there from downtown and come back. Oh, yeah. They had two. The North Shore and the Annecy Wilson. And, uh, and they didn't pay for the dollar, but you make $16 and $17 a night. That was good back in the 30s. Oh, yeah.
And 30s you played on his boat.
And, uh, who else was with you and Herb Moran on that boat?
Me, Moran, and then the two of the other. Tom, Tom, Tom, uh, Tom, his name was Tom. Ha! I know.
Tom. Tom. I bet I know. Tom. Tom. Yes. They told me about that. He's dead.
He's dead now. When did he die?
He died, oh, he's dead now, about ten years now.
Yeah, he died in Chicago. He went, he quit playing, went to the steel mill. Died, wake up at the steel mill. Oh, yeah. Yeah.
He quit playing in the, uh, in the middle 40s. Oh, yeah. Went to the steel mill.
